newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF approves fresh credit instalment for Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves fresh credit instalment for Ukraine.

text.p: International Monetary Fund experts have approved the latest instalment of a $100 million stand-by credit for Ukraine, the Fund's resident representative in the former Soviet republic said on Thursday.
"The board has completed a review on the basis of performance criteria and we expect the tranche by the end of the month," Alex Sundakov told Reuters.
The announcement of the August tranche followed a week-long visit by an IMF mission to Kiev, which also discussed a three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF) of $2.5 to $3 billion.
A decision will be made by the end of the year on that programme, which will succeed the $867 million stand-by programme agreed in May.

Ukraine has also requested a $1.5 billion currency stabilisation fund to support the new hryvnia currency introduced earlier this month. Officials say they want that credit to be extended as part of the EFF.
Sundakov said the next mission would visit Kiev next month or in November.

Fund missions have been visiting Ukraine each month to review economic progress and approve monthly disbursements under the stand-by programme. The IMF suspended credits for a time this year after the government overshot spending targets.
Ukraine has secured about $2 billion in IMF credits since winning approval for its market reform programme in 1994.

The 1997 budget, aimed at meeting IMF guidelines, calls for inflation to slow to 24.9 percent from a forecast this year of 48 percent and a reduction in the budget deficit to 2.4 percent of gross domestic product by Western calculations.
